### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional — no prior permission needed, but mandatory disclosure (not a ban) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is MDPI's publisher-wide AI policy (applies to all MDPI journals incl. Virtual Worlds; no Virtual Worlds-specific AI clause found). FACT: AI tools/LLMs (e.g. ChatGPT) cannot be listed as authors. FACT: authors may use generative AI for language editing/manuscript preparation/analysis support, but must disclose which tool (name, version) and how it was used — disclosure goes in Acknowledgments (which tool) and Materials & Methods (how used). No evidence of a per-journal permission gate requiring editor pre-approval; it is a disclose-after-use model, not a ban. Could not verify a Virtual Worlds-specific instructions-for-authors AI clause because mdpi.com/journal/virtualworlds/instructions returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; content above is drawn from MDPI's general research-ethics announcement plus secondary summaries (LinkedIn/LibGuides) of it, not a first-hand fetch of the journal's own instructions page. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/5687 |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes — MDPI (publisher-wide policy, Virtual Worlds included) permits prior posting to Preprints.org or other preprint servers before/during submission, as long as the preprint has not itself been peer-reviewed elsewhere and is disclosed (DOI + license) at submission; authors must not update the preprint version during confidential peer review.
> Source: https://www.mdpi.com/ethics

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** VR/AR/MR technology and applications papers, with a strong recent tilt toward applied/empirical studies: VR in education (360-degree video for undergraduate engagement), VR in healthcare/rehabilitation and psychology (reaction-time studies in high-school students), VR for social/wellbeing interventions (virtual choirs in care homes), and immersive systems/hardware (CAVE systems, corrections to prior CAVE work). Journal is quarterly, Scopus-indexed as of Aug 2025, no page-length restriction, welcomes 'as much experimental/theoretical detail as possible.'

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** empirical/experimental human-subjects studies (education, healthcare, psychology), systems/tools/software papers (VR/AR/MR hardware, CAVE, engines), applied case studies in industry, medicine, education, public space, HCI and human-agent interaction studies, reviews (journal explicitly welcomes review articles alongside original research)

Only publisher-reported aggregate ('6 weeks submission-to-publication', and a separately-found MDPI-wide 2026 median of '17.4 days to first decision' with no journal breakdown) — no first-hand author-reported review time for Virtual Worlds.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No source found anywhere (SciRev, forums, publisher pages) gives a desk-reject percentage for this journal.
